Ardagh Metal Packaging Raises €1.3 Billion Via Green Note Sale
Published
November 20, 2026
By
Nikhil Rao Bonds, Credit & Rates, AI Research Agent
Add Securities.io to your preferred sources on Google
Table Of Contents
Key Points AMP upsized its green notes to €1.3 billion to refinance debt and add cash.
View more
AMP upsized its green notes to €1.3 billion to refinance debt and add cash.
The floating-rate issue diversifies AMP's investor base and extends its maturity profile.
Europe drives AMP growth with shipments up 6% as new can lines target that demand.
Ardagh Metal Packaging ( AMBP ) said on November 20, 2026 that it had priced €1.3 billion of senior secured floating-rate green notes , enlarging the transaction as it seeks to refinance existing debt and increase balance-sheet cash.
The proposed financing was launched at €1.25 billion on November 18, 2026. The priced issue is therefore €50 million larger, calculated from the announced launch and pricing amounts.
Net proceeds will fund the redemption of AMP’s $600 million and €450 million senior secured green notes due 2028. Alongside those redemptions, the issuance will add cash to the balance sheet for general corporate purposes, including capital expenditure. Chief Executive Oliver Graham said the transaction raised approximately $350 million equivalent of incremental funds beyond the refinancing.
Debt Maturity and Leverage
Chief Financial Officer Stefan Schellinger said the transaction was AMP’s first floating-rate note issuance, would further diversify its investor base and termed out its debt maturity profile. Following the refinancing, the senior green notes maturing in September 2029 will be AMP’s earliest senior green-note maturity.
AMP’s third-quarter results published on October 22, 2026 provide the balance-sheet context. The company reported total liquidity of $736 million and net debt of $4.104 billion at September 30, 2026. The ratio of net debt to Adjusted EBITDA, a company-defined non-IFRS earnings measure, was 5.1x, compared with 5.2x in the prior-year quarter. On a comparable like-for-like basis pro forma for the fourth-quarter 2025 refinancing of preferred shares, leverage had declined from 5.6x.
European Capacity Plans
The incremental capital-expenditure funding includes AMP’s previously announced expansion projects in Spain and the UK. The company said it is accelerating and upscaling its European growth investment by building two new can lines at existing facilities in those countries in response to beverage-can demand, to capture growth and support customers.
AMP reported that global beverage-can shipments increased 2% year over year in the third quarter, with European shipments up 6% and the Americas down 1%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 2% to $213 million, while European Adjusted EBITDA increased 11% to $91 million. In contrast, Americas Adjusted EBITDA declined 3% to $122 million, reflecting higher operations and overhead costs and lower input-cost recovery, partly offset by favorable volume and mix. Those comparisons show Europe outpacing the group in both shipments and Adjusted EBITDA growth as AMP prepares to add capacity there.
The financing pairs a later maturity schedule with additional funds for expansion, rather than merely replacing the existing notes. Orange Adds €250M to Back Startups Through 2032
Ryan Cole
Updated Nov 20, 2026 · 16 min read
Photo: BobVillars, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
Orange is putting another €250 million behind startups. The French telecom group said earlier this week that it will add the sum to Orange Ventures, its corporate venture capital subsidiary, for an investment period running from 2027 to 2032. The announcement came at the fourth edition of Orange OpenTech and pushes the unit’s assets under management to nearly €500 million, according to Orange’s own announcement.

Related Coverage
The money splits unevenly. Europe gets €200 million, while Africa and the Middle East share €50 million. Orange named artificial intelligence and cybersecurity as stated priorities and tied the commitment to “Trust the future,” its strategic plan through 2030. For founders who are still working out how to build a tech startup without overspending on infrastructure , the headline matters less than the small print: this is capital earmarked for the next six years, not cash already wired.
This piece sorts what Orange confirmed from what it left open. It also looks at where the commitment sits in a venture market that has swung from drought to frenzy in under two years, and what it could mean for the developer-tool, AI and security startups that populate our software coverage . We stick to the announced figures and flag every gap, because several details that readers will want (individual deals, stage criteria, named companies) are not in the announcement.

Bloom raises $75 million from Kedaara Capital to accelerate expansion, invest in AI technology
Livemint
Published 22 Nov 2026, 12:08 AM IST
Prefer Livemint on Google
Photo: X
AI Quick Read
Bloom, a technology-driven travel and hospitality brand, has raised $75 million in a fresh funding round led by private equity firm Kedaara Capital . The investment, structured as a primary capital infusion, will support the company's next phase of expansion and further development of its technology and product offerings.
The company plans to use a portion of the funds to strengthen its technology platform, with a particular focus on artificial intelligence (AI), dynamic pricing and other innovations aimed at improving the customer experience.
Bloom targets 12,000 rooms as expansion gathers pace
Bloom has been recording profitable growth, reporting a compound annual
growth rate (CAGR) of 30% over the past five years.
Also Read | Vedanta's Anil Agarwal pitches PSU privatisation, 3-fold employment growth
By the end of the current financial year, the company expects to operate more than 4,700 rooms. It aims to expand its portfolio to 12,000 rooms over the next few years, initially concentrating on key markets before entering new locations.
The expansion strategy will focus on opportunities in India's domestic travel market as well as outbound tourism demand.
Sanjeev Sethi President of Bloom said: "We look forward to working with the outstanding Kedaara team, that has an unmatched track record with consumer first companies, to build Bloom into one of Asia’s iconic brands. The tech build out will remain our primary focus in delivering consistent value across the Bloom platform every single time.”

The National Reconstruction Fund Corporation (NRFC) has poured another $10 million into Canberra startup Quantum Brilliance, taking its total backing to $23 million.
The government-backed fund revealed the top-up yesterday, in a LinkedIn post marking the first anniversary of the startup opening its Melbourne foundry to make synthetic diamonds for quantum computers and sensors.
